subject: [video] R1 supports the PSNR-floor ruling with independent JPEG numbers (pan/static 36.4 dB at q90, 58.7 dB at q100)
body:
Independent evidence for the floor discussion, from a different codec (JPEG, no relation to the H.264 encoder). Same WP09 patterns, luma PSNR vs the source Y, our encoder vs libjpeg-turbo (cjpeg -baseline -dct int) on the identical content:
  pan 640x480    q90: ours 36.413 dB, cjpeg 36.439 dB ; q100: ours 58.686 dB
  static 178x146 q90: ours 36.463 dB, cjpeg 36.494 dB ; q100: ours 58.603 dB
  gradient/squares (smooth): q90 ours 50.58/50.48 dB.
So on pan/static the two independent encoders agree within 0.03 dB at q90 and both are far above 38 dB at q100, where the quantisation is nearly transparent. The 36 dB is the content (near-white-noise luma), exactly as WP09 says, not the encoder. For R1 I handled it by requiring the 38 dB floor on picture-like vectors and requiring parity with cjpeg on noise-like ones plus >=45 dB at q100; STATUS.md states the numbers. Same conclusion for the H.264 floors: a single absolute floor applied to every frozen pattern will fail conforming encoders; a per-pattern expectation or a lower floor on noise-like patterns is the honest fix. No change requested in any frozen file from me.
